items.title: Willie "Old Man" Parker Interview, 1958-11-07
items.q: I was getting in the car with a trombone player, Clement Tervalon

ctx.x: I had a band called the Eagle Brass Band uptown. Well he was trumpet, uh, strong and played with. Old big carnage. Was he playing Eureka too? Yeah. He, uh, this boy, this great trumpet player from the other corner, Lewis, Lewis what? What do you call it? Armstrong. Armstrong. Lewis and him lying together. And, you know, every time Armstrong meet, me, Darcony, he says, you're yet spitting in that trombone, you're yet to be kidding him, you know? He dead now, you know?

I saw his wife, uh, Friday. You did? She lives right around the corner from the Tulane Club. Yeah. I gotta go back and see her sometime. She seemed like a very nice lady. Yes, ma'am. I was getting in the car with a trombone player, Clement Tervalon, and she said, my husband used to play that instrument. Yeah. Willie Connish's wife. Willie Connish's wife. Just, just by being with a trombone player, I found her. Oh, uh. I was with, uh, this fella, Clement Tervalon. He works with Clement Tervalon. He's Burbank's…

Oh, on the street back. Yeah. Did you know Frankie Dooson? Oh, yes, sir, man. Well, he was a wonderful, uh, uh, what's it called, uh, rotina. Mm-hmm. He was a rotina Frankie Dooson. Tall, brown, silver. Well, where was he from?
